name: BottomNav
summary: Floating bar pinned to the bottom that holds an application's top-level navigation.

a11y.apg: No APG pattern covers site navigation, and that absence is the decision — the same one Sidebar records. What is adopted: native links inside a <nav>, natural Tab order, and aria-current="page" on the current item. What is deliberately NOT adopted is the Tabs pattern: a tab swaps a panel inside the page, a bottom bar changes page. Giving role="tablist" to a menu makes the screen reader promise arrow keys that lead nowhere. A page usually carries a Sidebar or a Topbar as well, so name the landmark when there is more than one.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: Enter and Space, which activate the focused destination. Space was delivered by the component and NOT declared before this measurement — the same direction as G-A11Y-04, and the reason this gate exists. Tab and Shift+Tab are out of the count on both sides by construction: Tab moves focus anywhere on a page, so it never distinguishes one component from another. What this measurement establishes is that there is no ENGINE keyboard here to measure — the keyboard is the document order, which is the correct answer for this component.

props.name: items
props.description: The navigation, as data — the SAME type Sidebar takes, on purpose: one list feeds the sidebar on desktop and the bar on the phone, and two lists of one menu drift apart. Each item is {id, label, href?, icon?, badge?, onClick?}. A nested `items` is ignored here: a bottom bar is flat. `badge` hangs off the icon's top corner and is sized against it (16px on a 24px icon, the ratio measured in shipping apps); pass an EMPTY badge (`badge: ""`) to get the plain dot that means "something new".

props.name: current
props.description: The id of the item you are on. It gets aria-current="page", which is also what the skin paints — one source for both, so they cannot drift apart.

props.name: variant
props.description: Where the BAR sits: floating as a loose pill, or edge against the screen with a hairline above it. It says nothing about how the current item is marked — that is `indicator`, and keeping the two apart is the whole point of the 20/08/2026 rewrite. The four names of 17/08/2026 (flat, surface, pill, dock) are still accepted and map onto the pair; they are deprecated, not removed.

props.name: indicator
props.description: The SHAPE that marks the current item. The meaning never changes with the shape: current is always the brand gold. `none` marks by colour alone; `subtle` and `pill` wrap icon and label in a tinted container and differ only in radius; the three circles wrap only the icon, by fill, by elevation or by a ring; `circle-bold` is the only solid fill, so it is the only one that flips the whole foreground. Every indicator keeps every label visible.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the floating pill is. `full` spans the screen minus the margin, as it always has; `content` sizes the pill to its items and centres it. Items then measure their own content instead of sharing the width equally, with the item's own touch target (--control-h-lg) as the minimum. Ignored on `edge`, which sits against the screen edge and stays full width.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the <nav>. Two navigation landmarks with the same name fail axe, and a page with a bottom bar usually has a Topbar or Sidebar too — name it.

notes: A dot badge (`badge: ""`) has NO accessible name — there is nothing to read. Put the meaning in the item's label instead: `label: <>Updates (new)`. A numbered badge announces itself.

The floating bar keeps clear of the iPhone home indicator with `margin-bottom: calc(--space-4 + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` — OUTSIDE the pill, since 0.8.8; before that the inset was padding and the pill grew down behind the system area. `edge` keeps it as padding, `max(--space-1, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`, because it sits against the edge. Either only has an effect if YOUR page declares `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">`; without it env() returns 0 and you get the normal spacing — it degrades, it does not break. Aurea does not write your meta tag.
Positioning is `sticky`, not `fixed`: it stays inside its container, so it cannot cover a page it does not own, and it falls back to static when there is nothing to scroll.
